source_locator: R392: p. 152-153; R643: listing under the LXVI Corps heading
current_activity: The 62nd Volksgrenadier Division moves into the line opposite the 424th Infantry toward Winterspelt
notes: Event date: CMH Ardennes ch. 7 p. 152: "At dusk on 15 December the 62d Volks Grenadier Division, forming the left of the LXVI Corps, had come into the lines opposite the left and center of the 424th Infantry"; p. 153: "the road to Winterspelt"; Nafziger 944GLAA (15 December 1944): "62nd Volks Grenadier Division: Oberst F. Kittel". Event definition: the move on 15 December and the attack on 16 December. Event support: two source families: CMH and Nafziger. Location: Winterspelt with a precision of 10 km, the village on the road named for the division advance. Location approximate: a village point. Location support: CMH names the road to Winterspelt. Commander: Oberst Friedrich Kittel. Opponents: US VIII Corps (106th Infantry Division, 424th Infantry).

location_qualifier: front opposite the Remagen bridgehead; battalion-size Kampfgruppen
current_activity: Contingents of the 62d Volksgrenadier Division are opposite the Remagen bridgehead by 17 March
notes: Event date: CMH The Last Offensive ch. 11 p. 232: "By 17 March the German order of battle opposite the bridgehead sounded impressive on paper"; "the Germans had brought in contingents of the 26th, 62d, 272d, 277th, and 326th Volks Grenadier Divisions; the 3d and 5th Parachute Divisions; and the 3d Panzer Grenadier Division". Event definition: the situation by 17 March. Event support: one source family (CMH). Location: Remagen with a precision of 25 km, the bridgehead named; CMH gives battalion-size Kampfgruppen and no division position. Location approximate: a representative point for the front opposite the bridgehead. Location support: CMH names the front opposite the bridgehead. Commander: unknown. Opponents: US III and VII Corps. Context: CMH ch. 11 p. 232 calls all these contingents battalion-size Kampfgruppen or units filled out with inexperienced replacements.
